title: restore-plan v1
description: What a host is handed to bring a fleet back (planning/migration-plan.html section 4). Sessions are authoritative and the layout is advisory (D3): the sessions list alone is enough to restore every session with its identity, directory and conversation, and the layout only arranges them. Every leaf of the layout is a slot, every slot names one session, and nothing in the plan is keyed by a pane number - the pane a slot lands in is recorded afterwards, as a realisation, never as identity. What this schema cannot say is checked by core/RestorePlan.ps1: every node is exactly a leaf or a container, every session's slot appears in the layout exactly once (sessions are never dropped), slots and session ids are unique, a parent names another session in the plan, a ratio lies strictly between 0 and 1, and a container has at least two children.

planId.description: Names this plan, e.g. 20260929-214500-horde. Not an identity of anything the plan restores.

sessions.description: Every session the plan restores. Authoritative: a host that can arrange nothing still restores each one.

slot.description: The name the layout uses for this session, unique in the plan. Never a pane number.

sessionId.description: The conversation id: the session's stable identity, unique in the plan.

agent.description: Which agent runs the session, e.g. claude or codex.

role.description: The native roles of core/roles.json; test/test-schema-restore-plan.ps1 fails if the two differ.

label.description: The session's fleet label, e.g. D or D1.

parent.description: The sessionId of the session that spawned this one. When present it names another session in this plan.

cwd.description: The directory the session runs in.

resume.description: How to bring the conversation back, produced by the agent's port so a host runs the command it is given without knowing each agent's flags.

layout.description: How the sessions are arranged: advisory. A host applies what it can after the engine has degraded the layout to its capabilities (section 4, Degradation rules).

advisory.description: Always true: the layout never decides which sessions exist.

name.description: Absent in a plan for a host with no workspaces: the engine has moved the name into the titles as a prefix.

tabs.description: One tab per window in a plan for a host with no tabs.

node.description: Either a leaf { slot } or a container { split, ratio?, children }. JSON Schema's subset here cannot say 'exactly one of the two', so core/RestorePlan.ps1 does.

slot.description: Leaf: the slot of a session in this plan.

split.description: Container: children side by side (right) or stacked (down), in order.

ratio.description: Container: the share of the first child, strictly between 0 and 1. Absent for a host with no sizes: dropped, never approximated.
